cert.note.model: Verified by substitution and simplification; no search required.
cert.note.unsat_core: Verifying requires re-solving, but only the core (far smaller).
cert.note.lp_dual.exact: Optimality certified in EXACT rationals: primal and dual feasibility plus c.x = b.y, all in Fraction. No tolerances and no trust in CBC.
cert.note.lp_dual.float: Weak duality in FLOATING POINT, with a tolerance. Fine for exploring; citing a constant needs exact mode.
cert.note.cegis: The list of counterexamples IS the certificate: it is the minimal set of inputs that pins this solution down.
cert.note.cnf_model: Checked clause by clause. No solver, no propagation.
cert.note.drat: Refutation proof. Checked by unit propagation (RUP/RAT): no SAT solver is involved, so the one that produced it need not be trusted.
cert.note.shrink_graph: Minimal (1-minimal), not minimum. `blocked` is the witness: every one-step reduction either fails a filter or satisfies the predicate. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.
cert.note.mus: Minimal unsatisfiable subset. The DRAT proof refutes the MUS and each witness is a model of the MUS without one of its clauses: together they certify unsatisfiability AND minimality without a solver.
cert.note.bisect: The threshold is certified by the pair that brackets it: a proof on the good side and a refutation on the bad side. Each is verified separately. MONOTONICITY in t is assumed, not proved.
cert.note.synth_proved: Two chained obligations: the bounded synthesis that found the candidate and the universal symbolic proof of it. Each is verified separately; the one that counts as a theorem is the second.
cert.note.sweep: Two different things: which family was examined (verifiable here) and whether the predicate was evaluated correctly on each graph (only if the predicate supplied a certificate: {certified} of {total} entries). COMPLETENESS of the family requires re-enumerating.
cert.note.graph_set: Verifies pairwise non-isomorphism and the filters. COMPLETENESS (that none is missing) can only be checked by re-enumerating.
verify.model.fails: the assignment does NOT satisfy the formula
verify.core.detail: core of {n} formulas (includes the negated claim)
verify.lp.exact.detail: EXACT rational arithmetic, no tolerances: optimum = {value}
verify.lp.float.detail: weak duality with a tolerance; to cite it, re-run in exact mode
verify.lp.float.warning: FLOATING-POINT certificate with tolerance 1e-6: not usable to cite an exact constant
verify.cegis.impl_ok: the implementation satisfies its own constraints
verify.drat.formula: the formula matches the declared one ({n} clauses)
verify.drat.steps: the proof is RUP/RAT step by step
verify.drat.detail: {steps} steps ({rup} RUP, {rat} RAT, {del} deletions) in {ms:.0f} ms
verify.sweep.stats: the statistics match the stored values
verify.sweep.detail: family of {n} graphs; does NOT verify completeness (that needs re-enumerating)

verify.sweep.unevaluated: {n} graphs were never evaluated (errors or inconclusive)

spec.no_function: {name} does not define a spec() function
engine.domain.proved: the predicate holds on all {count} items (FINITE DOMAIN, not the theorem)

Verifiable here: the ids are unique, the statistics match the stored values, and each predicate certificate checks out. NOT verifiable here: that the domain is complete or that the ids denote what they claim -- that is the spec's responsibility.

verify.family.programmable: {names} cannot be re-checked here: a programmable filter lives in the spec

verify.range.ordered: the sizes are in increasing order
verify.range.nothing_below: nothing failed below the first failure
verify.range.stopped: stopped at the first failure: the larger sizes were NOT examined

verify.matrix.inconclusive: {n} goals could not be proved; their column is empty, not false

The trace records the index taken into reduce() at each step, so verification replays the exact descent instead of re-running the search. `blocked` is the witness that no one-step reduction survives. Verifying requires the spec module, whose hash is included.

engine.farkas.found: {mode} certificate found: {n} hypotheses with a non-zero multiplier
engine.farkas.none: no {mode} certificate exists for this system
engine.farkas.not_polynomial: cannot be put in polynomial form: {detail}
engine.farkas.nonlinear_needed: the system is not linear. Re-run with --nonlinear (nonlinear=true over MCP), which is the nlinarith preprocessing, or use `prove`, which decides real arithmetic completely
engine.farkas.inexact: the multipliers could not be reconstructed as exact rationals, so there is nothing citable to emit
cert.note.farkas: Non-negative rational multipliers whose combination cancels every monomial and closes the system. Verified by multiplying and adding in Fraction: no solver, no search. This is what linarith emits; with nonlinear=true the extra rows are products and squares of the hypotheses, which is what nlinarith adds.

cert.note.proof: A proof assembled from lemmas. Each lemma carries its own certificate AND the link showing that what the certificate establishes entails the statement used downstream. Lemmas marked as bridges are verified but not linked: the step from what they establish to a formula is a modelling decision, and it is listed by name so the reader can weigh it.
verify.proof.link: lemma {name}: its certificate entails the statement used
verify.proof.step_link: the final step uses only the lemmas and the theorem's own hypotheses
verify.proof.unused: lemmas the theorem does not need: {names}

verify.ball.no_claim: no claim: the enclosure is the result
verify.ball.reproduced: re-evaluating the spec lands inside it

engine.prove.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses contradict each other, so this goal -- and every other goal -- follows. The proof is valid and says nothing. Run `check` on the hypotheses alone to find which pair clashes.
engine.farkas.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses close the system without the goal at all, so they are contradictory and any goal would have been proved.
verify.core.vacuous: VACUOUS: this core does not include the negated goal, so the hypotheses contradict each other and the proof holds for any goal.
verify.farkas.vacuous: VACUOUS: the hypotheses were found to close the system without the goal, so they are contradictory and any goal would follow. The certificate is valid and says nothing.
verify.proof.vacuous: VACUOUS: the lemmas contradict each other, so the theorem -- and any other -- follows from them. Check the lemma statements against each other before citing this.
cli.vacuous: the hypotheses are contradictory: this proof is vacuous

structures.too_symmetric: this family is too symmetric to canonicalise exactly on {n} points (over {cap} candidate relabellings). Refusing rather than returning a cheaper invariant: one that merged two non-isomorphic families would merge two orbits, and nothing downstream would notice
engine.induct.empty_base: the base is empty: k0={k0} is above base_upto={upto}
engine.induct.gap: the chain does not join: the step starts at k={step} but the base only reaches {upto}. Every n between them is proved by nothing
engine.induct.base_missing: base case k={k}: no certificate at {path}
engine.induct.base_invalid: base case k={k}: its certificate does not verify ({detail})
engine.induct.base_failed: base case k={k} was not established [{status}]: {detail}
engine.induct.bad_base: a base case must be a Spec, SweepSpec, DomainSpec, CNFSpec or a certificate path, not a {got}
engine.induct.step_failed: the inductive step was not proved [{status}]: {detail}
engine.induct.step_link: the step was proved, but what its certificate establishes does not entail the step statement
engine.induct.proved: {n} base cases k={k0}..{upto}, step from k={step}, chained by induction
engine.induct.conclusion: the property holds for every n >= {k0}
cert.note.induction: The induction schema, applied: a certificate per base case, a certificate for the step proved with the index FREE, and the two numbers that decide whether the chain joins. The schema itself is not a solver result and does not pretend to be one.
verify.induction.covered: the base cases are exactly k0..base_upto
verify.induction.joins: the step starts no later than the base ends
verify.induction.step_link: the step certificate entails the step statement
verify.induction.bridge: BRIDGE at k={k}: a finite check read as the property -- {why}
verify.induction.schema: The induction over the naturals is APPLIED here, not verified by a solver. It is one fixed schema, unlike a bridge, but it is still a step no certificate in this file performs.
verify.induction.detail: {n} base cases k={k0}..{upto}, plus the step
engine.sweep.no_canonicalize: --by-orbit needs the spec to declare canonicalize=, so there are orbits to sweep by
engine.sweep.not_invariant: the predicate is NOT invariant under the declared symmetry: {item} answers differently from its representative {rep}. Sweeping by orbit would have reported a verdict for {item} that it does not have. Drop --by-orbit, or fix canonicalize
cli.orbits.by_orbit: evaluated {evaluated} representatives, inferred {inferred}. INVARIANCE ASSUMED, not proved; {n} spot checks agreed.
verify.orbits.assumed: ASSUMED: only {evaluated} representatives were evaluated and the rest inferred, which needs the predicate to be invariant under the declared symmetry. That cannot be proved here; {n} spot checks against real non-representatives agreed with it.
verify.orbits.spot: the spot checks agree with their representatives
verify.sweep.replay.no_symmetry: the spec no longer declares a symmetry, so the inference cannot be reproduced

verify.witness.same_run: the witnesses minimise the sweep's own representatives

lean.lemma.derived: DERIVED and linked by certo, via `{engine}`. Its certificate entails this statement; what is left is to restate it in your own encoding and prove it.
lean.lemma.bridge: BRIDGE. Nothing proved this in Lean: {why}
lean.check.no_lake: no `lake` on PATH, so nothing compiled this. The file is emitted either way; it has simply not been checked
lean.check.no_project: {path} is not a Lean project (no lakefile), so `lake env lean` has no Mathlib to import. Emit into a project, or pass --lean-project
cli.lean.no_exporter: no deep Lean export for a {kind} certificate; `--lean` reads farkas, proof, sweep, domain_sweep and graph_set, and graph counterexamples come out as data
poly.budget.pairs: Buchberger gave up after {n} S-pairs: this ideal is too big for an exact computation here. Raise the budget, or reduce the number of variables
poly.budget.terms: a polynomial grew past {n} terms during the Groebner computation
numbers.not_prime: {n} is not prime, so there is no primality certificate for it
numbers.too_deep: the Pratt recursion went too deep at {n}
verify.pratt.complete: the factor list is all of {n}-1
verify.pratt.order: and no smaller order: {n} is prime
sos.no_numpy: numpy is not installed, so there is nothing to search for a Gram matrix with
sos.odd_degree: the polynomial has odd degree {d}, so it takes negative values and cannot be a sum of squares
sos.no_rounding: a numeric Gram matrix was found, but none of the {n} roundings survived exact re-verification. The search landed too close to the boundary of the PSD cone
cert.note.ideal: Cofactors h_i with f = sum h_i g_i. Finding them is a Groebner basis computation; checking them is expanding a product and comparing coefficients, in exact rationals. With f = 1 the system has no common solution over the complex numbers, hence over the reals, the rationals and the integers.
cert.note.sos: p = sum d_i q_i^2 with rational d_i and rational linear forms q_i. The Gram matrix was found in floating point and is not here -- it was the search. Checking this is multiplying polynomials.
cert.note.number: A Pratt primality tree: a witness generating (Z/n)^*, and a certificate for each prime factor of n-1, recursively down to 2. Checking it is modular exponentiation and nothing else.
verify.ideal.expands: the combination expands to the claim
verify.ideal.member: the claim vanishes on every common root
verify.ideal.field: This refutes solutions over the COMPLEX numbers, hence over the reals, rationals and integers too. The converse does not follow: had no certificate been found, a real solution would still not be implied.
verify.sos.expands: the squares add up to the polynomial
verify.sos.detail: a sum of {n} squares, in exact rationals
engine.ideal.inconsistent: the system has NO common solution: 1 is in the ideal, and the cofactors prove it
engine.ideal.member: the claim vanishes on every common root of the system, certified by {n} cofactors
engine.ideal.not_member: the claim does NOT follow from the equations: it is not in the ideal they generate. That is conclusive, not a timeout
engine.ideal.consistent: the system may have a solution: 1 is not in the ideal, so there is a common root over the complex numbers. Nothing here says whether a REAL one exists
engine.sos.found: a sum of {n} squares, exact, with denominator {denom}
engine.sos.none: no exact sum-of-squares certificate found. NOT a refutation: from degree 4 in 3 variables there are non-negative polynomials that are not sums of squares. {detail}
engine.number.prime: {n} is prime, with a Pratt certificate of {checks} modular checks
engine.number.composite: {n} is NOT prime, so there is no primality certificate: {detail}
engine.number.factored: {n} = {factors}, every factor with its own primality certificate
engine.opt.ilp_tight: integer optimum {value}, CERTIFIED: a feasible integral point achieves it and the exact dual bounds it there
engine.opt.ilp_gap: best integral point found: {value}. The exact dual bounds the optimum by {bound}, so the true optimum lies between them -- CBC's answer is not certified to be optimal
engine.opt.ilp_bound_only: no feasible integral point survived the exact check; all that is certified is the relaxation bound {bound}
verify.lp.ilp_bound: This is an ILP and no integral point travelled with it, so what is certified is the RELAXATION bound, not the integer optimum.
verify.lp.ilp_gap: The integral point achieves {value} and the dual bounds the optimum by {bound}. They differ, so the integer optimum is somewhere between and is NOT certified by this.
spec.bad_kind: {kind} is not a variable kind; known: {known}
engine.mixed.no_discrete: no discrete variables: declare some with kind='binary' or kind='integer', or use `opt`
engine.mixed.out_of_bounds: the search returned {var} outside its declared bounds once rounded
engine.mixed.residual_failed: the discrete choice leaves an infeasible continuous problem: {detail}
engine.mixed.inexact: the residual LP did not certify exactly, so nothing here would be citable
engine.mixed.infeasible: the rounded design violates {name} (and {n} constraints in total). The search's answer did not survive being checked exactly
engine.mixed.short: certified design reaching {value}, SHORT of the target {target} by {deficit}
engine.mixed.design: certified design reaching {value}; the relaxation bounds any design by {bound}
engine.mixed.optimal: certified design reaching {value}, which MEETS the relaxation bound: this is the global optimum
cert.note.mixed_design: A discrete skeleton, the exact continuous packing inside it, and what the two attain. Certified: the assignment is integral and in range, the full point satisfies every original constraint exactly, the residual LP is that problem with this assignment substituted, and its dual is exact. NOT certified, unless the achieved value meets the relaxation bound: that this skeleton is the best one.
verify.mixed.integral: the discrete assignment really is discrete
verify.mixed.feasible: the full point satisfies every original constraint
verify.mixed.value: it attains the value it claims
verify.mixed.residual: the residual LP's own certificate holds
